title: Affinity-guided changelog composer and manifest affinity stamps
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: make variant rollouts and capacity planning faster by surfacing runtime affinity signals on model manifests and by auto-drafting concise, priority-sorted changelog blurbs. This PR adds an opt-in 'affinity_stamp' metadata to manifests (hardware_family, os_kernel_tag, expected_latency_bucket), a small composer service that merges onboarding diffs with occupancy and sample-sufficiency heuristics to produce release snippets, and a migration/backfill tool that infers affinity from recent perf snapshots. The composer emits short human-readable blurbs and structured 'rollout_advisory' labels that downstream SRE and release automation can consume. Backwards compatibility: manifests without affinity_stamp are accepted and treated as 'affinity: unknown'. Feature-flagged rollout with dry-run and canary namespace. Linear links: ENG-10111 and ENG-9142. Related to automated release notes initiative ENG-8723 and SRE request SUP-321.

release_notes: Add manifest affinity_stamp (schema v2) that records runtime signals; introduce an affinity-guided changelog composer that drafts prioritized release blurbs and rollout advisories using occupancy and sample heuristics. Includes a backfill tool to infer affinity from perf snapshots. Feature-flagged and backward compatible.
testing: Unit tests for schema and composer added. Backfill dry-run against staging completed. Canary e2e validated manifest ingestion with affinity_stamp. Observed ~2% additional CPU on writer under 500rps due to light parsing.
